24	## Findings
25	
26	### Robustness
27	
28	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
29	  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
30	  in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers
31	  bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
32	  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
33	  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
34	  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
35	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around
36	  `Negotiator.setup` or `move`. Fields a hidden case may lack crash it: a rival quote without
37	  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`
38	  (`writer.py` `FIELDS`), a scorecard without `quarter` (`claims.py` `scorecard`), a month not in
39	  `YYYY-MM` (`months_back`). The session then sits until the wave cap, which scores the
40	  alternative (0 in D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17). → Catch per move; on error send our last
41	  sheet again with the template e-mail.
42	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One error stops the final.** `runner.play_waves` re-raises any non-403
43	  `ArenaError` from the case-list poll, and a network error after the client's retries is not
44	  caught at all (`arena_kit/client.py` `_call`). Every later wave is then lost; no human may
45	  restart. → Catch everything in the poll loop, log, sleep, poll again; a crashed case resumes
46	  with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` (a second `POST` is a 409 naming the session).
47	
48	### Timing
49	
50	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Four bidders or more time out.** The arena answers one call per session at
51	  a time (`arena_kit/client.py`: "a call may wait for another call on the same session first").
52	  Supplier replies took 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves in `logs/runs/`); our writer 1.8 s
53	  median, 6.3 s max (73 calls, none failed, 7 dropped by the filter). A thread waits about
54	  (N - 1) x 21 s for its next message against a 60 s limit:
55	
56	  | Bidders | Wait at median | Wait at p90 | Rounds per thread in 390 s |
57	  |---|---|---|---|
58	  | 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 9 / 6 |
59	  | 3 | 44 s | 66 s, late | 6 / 4 |
60	  | 4 | 65 s, late | late | 5 / 3 |
61	
62	  P05 (3 bidders) had one late move in v5. No case file has more than 3 bidders, but hidden
63	  cases bring "new settings". → With 4 or more bidders, stop sending to the clearly worst ones
64	  after round 1; the writer's 20 s timeout matters little next to the supplier's reply time.
65	
66	### Data and the Sunday release
67	
68	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The release reaches only part of the agent.** `DataPackage` finds
69	  `data/release-sunday/` next to the package, merges its `facts.json` (new IDs only) and puts its
70	  `data/*.csv` rows into the ID index for `lookup` and `ids`, never into SQLite
71	  (`arena_kit/data.py`, `_ids`). `personas.profile()`, `Negotiator.full_cost()` and the claims
72	  built from SQL (`po_lines`, `cost_drivers`, `documents`, `suppliers`) never see release rows,
73	  and document files resolve against the package root, not the release. Release IDs can still be
74	  cited. `design.md` says the release is "read at runtime"; that holds for `facts.json` only.
75	  → Read release rows through `pkg.ids(prefix)` / `pkg.lookup` (each row carries `root`) in
76	  `profile()` and the document claims. Check the CSV schema at 08:00.
77	- 2026-10-10 `data` **Most suppliers have no text.** Of 447 suppliers, 46 have documents, 31 news,
78	  18 quote remarks; the other 401 get the neutral profile (rate 7 %, no signals). A new supplier
79	  in the final is one of them or unknown to the package. → Its own e-mails and the release are
80	  the only persona source.
81	- 2026-10-10 `data` 15 of 108 quotes are priced per 100 (13) or per 1000 (2) pieces
82	  (`quotes.price_unit`). Rival-quote and order-history claims compare `unit_price` with the
83	  supplier's per-piece price without converting. → Divide by `price_unit` before comparing.
84	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Structures only in unplayed cases** (case files): `tooling_eur` negotiable
85	  and lead time at most 84 days (P06), chargeback in the alternative (P12), index series PPI-C241
86	  in a clause (P16), fixed payment in a quality case (P12), a 3-part bundle (P15). Every case type
87	  and category goal appears in at least one hosted case. Only `incoterm` (D02) lies outside the
88	  fields the planner knows.
89	
90	### Persona signals
91	
92	- 2026-10-10 `data` **The patterns are not fitted to the practice suppliers**: the package's text
93	  is generated and its phrases recur, so all 10 suppliers of the unplayed cases get at least one
94	  trait. They miss other forms of the same phrases: "restructuring programme with its banks"
95	  (sup:70150), "negotiating with its banks" (sup:70280), "lowered its rating" (sup:70310),
96	  "bought their nickel and alloys forward" (sup:70730), "advertising free machine capacity"
97	  (sup:70250), "allocated in line with last year's call-offs" (sup:70410). "I cannot sign
98	  anything that lowers our margin now" (5 call notes) is a trait with no pattern. → Widen to word
99	  stems before the release adds new wording.
100	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Supplier e-mails carry traits too:** 13 of 220 supplier e-mails in
101	  `exports/messages.jsonl` match `SIGNALS` (price_frozen sup:70530; spare_capacity sup:70210,
102	  70250, DEMO-J1; capacity_full sup:70240; cash_need sup:70210), including a sandbox supplier the
103	  package does not know. → Scanning each reply gives unknown suppliers a profile (untested in
104	  play).
105	
106	### Tuning
107	
108	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Out-of-sample performance is unmeasured.** The 0.727 mean is in-sample:
109	  every constant was tuned on the same ten hosted cases and the other nine cannot be played.
110	  Runs of one case spread widely across v1 to v6 (P18 0.25 to 0.49 over seven runs, P08 0.40 to
111	  0.55), and with a model-written paragraph the wording changes per run while wording moves the
112	  price (`learnings.md`, takeaway 3). → Treat single-run moves below about 0.1 as noise.
113	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Evidence behind each constant** in `buyer/policy.py` (from `git log -p`):
114	
115	  | Constant | Cases behind it | Risk |
116	  |---|---|---|
117	  | `ANCHOR` leverage 0.78 | P05, P08 / P18 (one template) | medium |
118	  | `ANCHOR` routine 0.82 | P07 (P04 overridden by price_frozen) | medium to high |
119	  | `ANCHOR` quality_first 0.88 | P11 | medium |
120	  | `ANCHOR` stabilise 0.92, secure_supply 0.88 | none: always overridden in practice | high, untested |
121	  | `FRACTION` 0.3 | D01, D02, all hosted cases | low |
122	  | `DEEP` 0.06 | P05 (two job shops), D02 | medium |
123	  | price_frozen 0.95 | P03, P04 | low to medium |
124	  | capacity_full 0.93, budget 0.16, overtime 0.005 | P10, P05 sup:70240 | medium |
125	  | `near_cost` 0.97, budget 0.14 | P02 | high |
126	
127	  → A hidden `stabilise` or `secure_supply` case with no override opens at an anchor never played.
128	
129	## Sunday 08:00 checklist
130	
131	1. `uv run arena data`; confirm `DataPackage("data/package").release` is not `None`.
132	2. List the release's `data/*.csv` and their columns; count supplier IDs new vs in the package.
133	3. Run every case file through `arena-sim` again with the release loaded.

28	| 3 | **Concede in currencies, not price:** hold one or two terms it values back from round 1 and spend one per round as our move | concessions are only answered after a move; logrolling moves price without paying price | sandbox, then P07 / P08 |
29	| 4 | **Spend patience in fewer, larger steps** | the bot gives back only 0.2 to 0.7 of each step and stops on a cumulative gap; many small steps burn patience without buying price | sweep `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on the sandbox (free) |
30	| 5 | **Expected-value acceptance after `final_offer`** | pushing after `final_offer` walked once (D01); the gain from one more step is small | already behind `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL`; decide from data |
31	| 6 | **Persona playbook** (table below): the right currency per supplier type | procurement practice and our persona signals agree | per case, one change per batch |
32	| 7 | **Writing rules for LLM counterparts:** warm, questions, reasons, trades, a story for the boss | largest LLM negotiation study: warmth and questions close deals, dominance causes impasses | wording only; check replies' back office |
33	
34	What not to do: extreme anchors (walk-aways roughly triple), threats and dominance, bluffed
35	urgency or rivals, repeating an unchanged sheet, and anything that targets the bot's prompt
36	(prompt injection is an attack under the rules).
37	
38	## 1. How the arena's suppliers concede
39	
40	From the price paths of every logged thread (script logic: supplier price per reply, our price per
41	message, statuses). Values for the current engine's practice runs:
42	
43	| Case | Supplier type | Anchor below quote | Its first move | Its step per our step (ρ) | Σ gap at `final_offer` | Deal below quote | Score |
44	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
45	| P07 | routine, family | 18 to 19 % | 2.6 to 3.5 % | 0.3 to 0.7 | 0.12 to 0.19 | 5.6 to 6.8 % | 0.73 to 0.75 |
46	| P08 | leverage, distributor | 21 % | 8 to 10 % | 0 to 1.0 | 0.09 to 0.23 | 7.3 to 11.6 % | 0.40 to 0.55 |
47	| P18 | leverage, distributor | 22 % (7 % once) | 7 to 10 % | 0 to 0.9 | 0.09 to 0.14 | 8.2 to 13.1 % | 0.25 to 0.49 |
48	| P01 | stabilise, price increase | 9 % | 2.4 to 3.5 % | 0.4 to 0.9, then 2 | 0.08 to 0.10 | 5.2 to 6.0 % | 0.90 to 0.97 |
49	| P11 | quality first, cash short | 12 % | 0 to 2 % | 0.3 to 0.6, then 0 | 0.15 to 0.18 | 3.2 % | 0.71 |
50	| P10 | secure supply, fully booked | 7 % | 1.6 % | 0.1 to 0.2 | 0.015 | 1.9 to 2.2 % | 0.67 to 0.68 |
51	| P02 | stabilise, near cost | 5 % (7 % walked) | -0.7 % | 0.05 to 0.4 | 0.03 | about 0 % | 0.46 to 0.51 |
52	| P03, P04 | price frozen | 4 % | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0 | 0.04 to 0.06 | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0.86 to 0.92 |
53	
54	Findings:
55	
56	1. **The first counter carries the deal.** In P08 and P18 its first counter already holds 75 to
57	   100 % of the final cut, in P07 and P01 about half. Later rounds add 0 to 4 points of the quote.
58	2. **It answers our steps at ρ < 1.** If we close the gap fully, the deal lands at
59	   `c1 - ρ / (1 + ρ) * (c1 - anchor)`: with ρ = 0.4 at 71 % of the way from our anchor to its first
60	   counter. Observed: 73 to 90 %, because `final_offer` usually comes before the gap closes.
61	3. **ρ grows late** (D01: 0.2 early, 1 to 2 in the last rounds), the time-dependent part of the
62	   tactic. `final_offer` cuts this off before we reach it.
63	4. **`final_offer` arrives early:** after 2 to 6 of our messages, at a cumulative gap of 0.09 to
64	   0.23 of its price (0.015 for the fully booked P10). The round limit never binds. The traces
65	   cannot yet separate a patience budget from a floor that our claims move (the same supplier
66	   stopped at 5.35 to 5.61 in P08 depending on our path, which points to patience).
67	5. **A shallow anchor gives a shallow first counter:** P18 opened at 7 % below and got 6.6 %, the
68	   worst run (0.25); at 22 % below it got 8 to 10 %.
69	6. **Pushing past `final_offer` risks the deal:** D01 walked away after one more sheet below its
70	   final (`D01_212404b7930bfc68`).
71	
72	Consequences: the literature's default against unknown opponents (Boulware, hold early, concede
73	late) assumes the opponent keeps playing to the deadline. Ours does not, so its advice inverts:
74	win in round 1, then close the gap in few, deliberate steps before patience runs out.
75	
76	## 2. Opening and anchoring
77	
78	**Research.** The first offer anchors the settlement (Galinsky and Mussweiler 2001; NegotiationArena
79	found opening offers correlate with final prices, rho about 0.72, for LLM agents too). Precise
80	numbers anchor harder than round ones and signal preparation (Mason et al. 2013; Loschelder et al.
81	2017). Extreme offers backfire: 30 % walk-aways after an extreme opening against 11 % after a
82	moderate one (Schweinsberg et al. 2012), confirmed in a 2018 replication. The anchor loses power
83	when the recipient focuses on its own alternatives and target (Galinsky and Mussweiler).
84	
85	**For us.**
86	- Keep the goal-based anchors (`ANCHOR` in `buyer/policy.py`: 0.78 leverage to 0.92 stabilise);
87	  they sit at the edge the research and our 20 vs 30 % sandbox test agree on. Never above 25 %
88	  below the quote.
89	- Make the anchor precise (4.76, not 4.75) and give it one reason the supplier can check: its own
90	  past price, a falling driver, a rival offer. Already true for the figures; keep the reason next
91	  to the price in the e-mail.
92	- Do not open shallow out of politeness: P18 at 7 % below was the worst run.
93	
94	## 3. Multi-issue offers: MESOs and logrolling
95	
96	**Research.** Multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (Leonardelli, Gu, McRuer, Medvec and
97	Galinsky 2019, six experiments) give stronger anchors, better outcomes for the offerer, more joint
98	gain and a friendlier relationship than one package; recipients read them as sincere. Guidance:
99	three offers, equal value to us, different mixes, all at or better than our target; the choice
100	reveals the counterpart's priorities. Automated negotiation does the same on iso-utility curves:
101	offer packages of equal own value and pick the one closest to the opponent's last offer (Faratin,
102	Sierra and Jennings 2002; Lai and Sycara). Package deals ("nothing agreed until everything is
103	agreed") turn a price fight into trades.
104	
105	**For us.** The arena allows three sheets per message and the bot picks one and answers it
106	(`learnings.md`). Today we send one sheet per message.
107	
108	- **Round 1: three sheets of equal C**, each at the anchor's C, varying the terms where the
109	  supplier's value differs from ours: payment days (its cost of money), contract length, lead
110	  time, ppm headroom, start date. `eco.plan_terms` already ranks term sets; take the best three
111	  distinct ones and set each price so C is equal.
112	- **Read the pick:** the chosen sheet tells us its priority; carry those terms forward (`adopt`
113	  already takes over terms from its counters).
114	- **Later rounds:** one sheet is enough unless a new lever opened. A second sheet that trades a
115	  term for price on its preferred axis is cheap information.
116	- Hold the walk-away and must-haves on every sheet: three sheets mean three chances for it to
117	  agree, so each one must be a deal we want (an `agreed` freezes the price).
118	
119	## 4. Conceding: currency, size and pace
120	
121	**Research.** ANAC winners pair a tough bidding curve with an opponent model and a lenient
122	acceptance near the deadline (Baarslag et al.; Fawkes 2013; Agent K 2010 extrapolates the opponent
123	from the mean and spread of its offers). Shrinking concessions make the counterpart expect a limit
124	and counter less ambitiously (Tey, Schaerer, Madan and Swaab 2021, seven studies). Deadline
125	research: agreements cluster at the deadline (Roth, Murnighan and Schoumaker 1988), but here the
126	supplier's own patience is the effective deadline. Procurement practice: never give a concession
127	without asking for something specific in return.
128	
129	**For us.**
130	- **Concede in currencies the supplier values and we do not.** The bot gives nothing without a
131	  move from us; a move need not be price. Candidates by case, priced with `total_cost` and its
132	  `supplier_value`: a 24-month term where it is free to us (P03, P04, P07, P10), forecast and
133	  volume statements, ppm headroom below the must-have (P11: 300 ppm costs us about 7 EUR per ppm
134	  point a year; 1000 ppm would cost about 0.31 EUR per unit, which the supplier may value more),
135	  a later start where we are indifferent, faster payment only for suppliers whose rate exceeds
136	  our 8 %. Today `plan_terms` gives all of these in round 1. Hold back one or two and release
137	  one per round as the move, with the price step smaller or zero. Hypothesis: same final price
138	  with less patience spent.
139	- **Fewer, larger price steps.** With ρ between 0.2 and 0.7 and a cumulative-gap stop, our
140	  `FRACTION = 0.3` closes the gap slowly and pays patience for every open round. Sweep 0.3 / 0.5 /
141	  0.7 on the sandbox, which costs no quota.
142	- **Shrink our steps visibly** (Tey et al.): the supplier reads them as our limit. Our steps
143	  already shrink; keep it, and say in words which step is the last.
144	- **Never move on a round where it did not move**, except with a currency (holding is free; an
145	  unchanged sheet is "My call: hold" for both sides).
146	
147	## 5. Acceptance and the end of a thread
148	
149	**Research.** The standard rule is AC_next: accept when its offer is at least as good as what we
150	would send next (most common in ANAC, Baarslag et al.); winners add a time rule that relaxes near
151	the deadline. Bargaining theory gives the expected-value form: accept now when
152	`C_now <= (1 - p) * E[C_next] + p * C_alt`, with p the chance the next push ends the thread.
153	
154	**For us.**
155	- AC_next is in place (`theirs <= ours[-1]` accepts). Keep it.
156	- After `final_offer`, p is high (one walk in our pushes so far) and the expected gain of one more
157	  step is small (0 to 1 % in our traces). Accept unless `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` data shows a net gain
158	  across several cases; in cases without an alternative (D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17) never push.
159	- Prepare the worst acceptable sheet before message 9 so a late `final_offer` can be taken at once.
160	
161	## 6. Estimating the floor
162	
163	**Research.** Bayesian learning of the reservation price (Zeng and Sycara 1998), regression on the
164	opponent's concession curve (Hou 2004), Gaussian-process prediction of its next offers (IAMhaggler,
165	Williams et al. 2011). With three counters p1, p2, p3 and geometric decay, Aitken's formula gives
166	the limit: `R = p3 - (p3 - p2)^2 / ((p3 - p2) - (p2 - p1))`. Known failure: when step ratios rise
167	(slower than geometric) it underestimates the floor and pushes too hard. Every observed counter is
168	a hard upper bound on the floor.
169	
170	**For us.** Useful as a secondary signal, not a stop rule: the bot stops on patience before its
171	floor, so a floor estimate mostly tells us whether a relationship charge is near (stabilise,
172	secure supply) and whether a large first concession means room (already `DEEP` in the policy).
173	The relationship charge in a finished practice result gives the supplier's true margin and cost
174	(`learnings.md`), which beats any curve fit for practice cases.
175	
176	## 7. Procurement levers by supplier situation
177	
178	**Research** (practice literature: Kraljic 1983, consultancy and CIPS sources; conventions, not
179	studies): classify the position first (leverage: compete and push price; bottleneck and strategic:
180	secure supply and joint value); answer a price-increase letter with a line-item breakdown weighted
181	by each driver's cost share; accept justified increases only index-linked or temporary; price
182	payment terms at both sides' cost of money; index clauses with a deadband of 3 to 5 %, a lag,
183	a cap, both directions and only the exposed cost share; threaten a second source only if it is
184	real; agree chargebacks before the dispute. Preferred-customer research (Schiele et al.): suppliers
185	reward attractive customers with capacity and price; forecast visibility and payment reliability
186	are what they ask for most. Collaborative but assertive buyers realise more value (Vantage
187	Partners survey, correlational).
188	
189	**Playbook**, joined with our persona signals (`learnings.md`, Persona signals):
190	
191	| Situation | Signal in the data | Give | Ask | Avoid |
192	|---|---|---|---|---|
193	| Cash short | "bank is watching", "pay earlier", cash discount | faster payment when its rate beats our 8 % (cash discounts imply 37 to 56 %/yr) | price | ignoring its ask when payment is fixed: say so and offer the next best currency |
194	| Fully booked | "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | its lead time, a firm 24-month volume, forecast | price at its standard speed | deep anchors (P10 patience 0.015), paying overtime for speed we do not value |
195	| Spare capacity | "second shift on hold" | volume, extra parts, long term | price | |
196	| Price frozen | "no room on price", "price list applies to all" | nothing on price | payment days, contract length, freight, start date | price pushes (no move, only lost patience) |
197	| Approval ladder | "above 2 % need the approval" | small steps (2 % or less), a reason the rep can forward to its boss | | one big ask that goes to a committee |
198	| Index-driven distributor | material share in its quote, clause offered | contract length only with a clause we can live with | deadband, share limited to material, falling series only | taking a 0 % deadband clause on a rising series (P02: score 0) |
199	| Price increase letter | letter above its drivers' index move | the index-weighted justified part, later start | notice period, start date, split | citing indices that rose (they confirm its case) |
200	| Stabilise, near cost | own-plant should-cost close to the quote | the price with the lowest C incl. relationship charge | terms | squeezing below sustainable margin (charge grows with the square) |
201	| Quality first | high scorecard ppm | | low ppm commitment, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` | trading quality away for price unless C says so |
202	
203	## 8. RFQs with two or three bidders
204	
205	**Research.** Competition is worth more than negotiating skill: one extra bidder beats an optimally
206	negotiated deal (Bulow and Klemperer 1996). For complex, non-standard contracts, negotiation beats
207	a pure price auction because terms differ per bidder (Bajari, McMillan and Tadelis 2009). One
208	best-and-final round works; repeated ones teach bidders to hold back (practice sources).
209	
210	**For us.** The current design matches: compare bids on total C, cite the cheapest rival's real
211	standing offer (a new argument every round), keep losing threads alive as the alternative.
212	Additions: one explicit best-and-final message per bidder near the end, not several; push the
213	bidder with the lowest C first and keep others warm with a question about capacity or delivery.
214	P05 is at 0.83, so RFQs are not where the points are.
215	
216	## 9. Writing for LLM counterparts
217	
218	**Research.** The largest AI negotiation competition (Vaccaro et al. 2025, about 120k to 180k
219	negotiations): warm agents beat cold ones on deal rate, joint value and counterpart satisfaction;
220	dominance claimed value but raised impasses; positivity, gratitude and questions predicted deals.
221	Buyers are harder for LLMs than sellers, and splitting a coded offer generator from an LLM narrator
222	lifted buyer deal rates from 27 % to 89 % (OG-Narrator, Xia et al. 2024): our architecture.
223	Asking about interests improves joint outcomes even when only one side does it (Thompson 1991).
224	Disappointment draws concessions, anger backfires on value disputes (Van Kleef). Objective
225	criteria and trades over positions (Fisher and Ury). LLMs drift toward a user who argues a side
226	(sycophancy rose from 50 to 79 % in one benchmark): a calm, reasoned position held over rounds
227	can move them, which is persuasion, not injection.
228	
229	**Writing rules** for `buyer/writer.py` and the paragraph prompt in `buyer/llm.py`:
230	
231	1. Open with one sentence that acknowledges its last message, specifically (what it moved, what it
232	   asked for).
233	2. Answer every request it made, even with no: "Payment terms are fixed in this agreement; what
234	   we can offer instead is ..." (P11).
235	3. One or two reasons per message, each a checkable fact next to its ID; more reasons dilute.
236	4. Frame every move as a trade: "If you can do X, we can do Y."
237	5. Ask one open question about its constraints ("What would make a price near X work for your
238	   planning?"). No "why" questions.
239	6. Express disappointment at the gap, never anger at the person.
240	7. Give the rep a forwardable rationale for its boss: figure, source, what we give in return.
241	8. Name our last step as last, once, and mean it.
242	9. No urgency, budget, target or missing alternative; no threats; no fake rivals; nothing aimed at
243	   the bot's instructions.
244	
245	## 10. Experiment plan
246	
247	The sandbox (D01, D02) is free and deterministic, so one run per variant measures the change.
248	Practice quota only for changes that won there; one change per batch.
249	
250	| Order | Experiment | Where | Read out |
251	|---|---|---|---|
252	| 1 | `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 | D01, D02 | final price, rounds to `final_offer`, Σ gap |
253	| 2 | Round 1 with three equal-C sheets against one | D01, D02, then P07, P08, P18 | first counter, which sheet it picked |
254	| 3 | Hold back one currency (contract length or forecast) for round 2 or 3 | D01, then P07, P10 | its step after a currency move against a price move |
255	| 4 | Explicit answer to its stated need | P11 | price after round 2; back office tone |
256	| 5 | ppm headroom as currency | P11 | price per ppm point given against our 7 EUR |
257	| 6 | `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` | cases with an alternative only | walks against gain |
258	
259	Record each result in `learnings.md` (tag `arena`), including the ones that fail.
260	
261	## Sources and confidence
262	
263	High: our own traces (`logs/sessions/`, every number in section 1 recomputed from them).
264	Medium: peer-reviewed results read from abstracts or reliable summaries. Low: practitioner and
265	vendor sources, conventions rather than evidence; numbers in section 7 are of this kind.
266	
267	- Galinsky and Mussweiler 2001, first offers as anchors, JPSP 81(4): https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/4593e56e2f94f5ffc75789ddacdfbe3670481cbe
268	- Mason, Lee, Wiley and Ames 2013, precise offers, JESP 49(4): https://business.columbia.edu/press-release/cbs-press-releases/new-research-shows-asking-precise-not-round-number-during
269	- Schweinsberg, Ku, Wang and Pillutla 2012, extreme anchors, JESP 48: https://www.martinschweinsberg.com/content/files/2022/03/Publication-2012-Schweinsberg-Ku-Wang-Pillutla-JESP-in-press.pdf
270	- Tey, Schaerer, Madan and Swaab 2021, decreasing concessions, OBHDP 165: https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jobhdp/v165y2021icp153-166.html
271	- Leonardelli et al. 2019, MESOs, OBHDP 152: https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jobhdp/v152y2019icp64-83.html ; guide: https://www.pon.harvard.edu/daily/business-negotiations/how-to-use-mesos-in-business-negotiations
272	- Faratin, Sierra and Jennings 2002, similarity-based trade-offs, AI 142: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/entities/publication/fc2ffe91-2e01-463e-a64b-8b633e74c5ba
273	- Baarslag et al., acceptance conditions and BOA: https://homepages.cwi.nl/~baarslag/pub/Acceptance_conditions_in_automated_negotiation.pdf ; https://homepages.cwi.nl/~baarslag/pub/Decoupling_Negotiating_Agents_to_Explore_the_Space_of_Negotiation_Strategies.pdf
274	- Baarslag et al. 2016, learning about the opponent: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10458-015-9309-1
275	- Zeng and Sycara, Bayesian learning in negotiation: https://cdn.aaai.org/Symposia/Spring/1996/SS-96-01/SS96-01-019.pdf
276	- Williams et al. 2011, IAMhaggler: https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/11/Papers/080.pdf
277	- Roth, Murnighan and Schoumaker 1988, deadline effect (via): https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/experimental-economics/article/bargaining-under-time-pressure-from-deadlines/F388EC46629F094DDB48A96AE00F8DCC

279	- Bajari, McMillan and Tadelis 2009, auctions versus negotiations in procurement: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=414255

# Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
- `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  `urgency`).
- `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.

## sessions

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |

"""Round 1 per session: our claims (refs), its claim verdicts and its first counter."""
import glob
import json
import sys

pat = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "P*"
for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"logs/sessions/practice/{pat}_*.json")):
    d = json.load(open(path))
    r = d["result"]
    tr = r["trace"]
    sups = {m["actor"] for m in tr if m["actor"] != "buyer"}
    if len(sups) != 1:
        continue
    b1 = next((m for m in tr if m["actor"] == "buyer" and m["round"] == 1), None)
    s1 = next((m for m in tr if m["actor"] != "buyer" and m["round"] == 1), None)
    s0 = next((m for m in tr if m["actor"] != "buyer" and m["round"] == 0), None)
    if not b1 or not s1:
        continue
    mv = b1["move"]
    sheets = [s["terms"] for s in mv.get("term_sheets") or []]
    body = mv.get("body") or mv.get("text") or ""
    verdicts = [(c.get("status") or c.get("result"), c.get("refs")) for c in s1["move"].get("claim_results") or []]
    reasons = [x for x in s1.get("reasons") or [] if "checked" in x or "verified" in x or "took" in x]
    print(f"\n{path.split('/')[-1]} score={r.get('score', 0):.3f} q={s0['move']['terms'].get('unit_price')} -> c1={s1['move']['terms'].get('unit_price')} ({s1['move'].get('status')})")
    print("  sheets:", sheets)
    print("  refs:", mv.get("refs"))
    print("  verdicts:", verdicts)
    for x in reasons:
        print("   ", x[:160])
    para = [ln for ln in body.split("\n") if ln.strip()][2:4]
    print("  words:", " ".join(para)[:600])

import os

RETRY_STATUS = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
CALLS_PER_SECOND = 9  # the arena allows 10 per key; stay just below, across all threads
# A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute (its time does not count against your 60 s),
# and a call may wait for another call on the same session first: wait long enough for both.
TIMEOUT_S = 180.0
# Practice has a daily quota per team: every practice session start carries what is left in this
# header, and GET /v1/me tells where the team stands.
REMAINING_HEADER = "X-Practice-Remaining"
ME_PATH = "/me"
# A 429 with a short Retry-After is the per-second rate limit: wait and retry. Any other 429 (the
# practice quota, too many open sessions) does not go away by retrying.
MAX_RETRY_AFTER_S = 5


class ArenaError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int, detail):
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}: {detail}")
        self.status, self.detail = status, detail


class ArenaClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url=None,
        api_key=None,
        *,
        retries=3,
        transport=None,
        timeout=TIMEOUT_S,
        rate=CALLS_PER_SECOND,
    ):
        base_url = (base_url or os.environ.get("ARENA_URL", "")).rstrip("/")
        if not base_url:
            raise ValueError("set ARENA_URL (e.g. https://…) or pass base_url")
        key = api_key or os.environ.get("ARENA_API_KEY")
        headers = {"X-API-Key": key} if key else {}
        self.retries, self.rate, self._lock, self._next = retries, rate, threading.Lock(), 0.0

"""What the supplier's e-mail asks of us. The bots write their asks in a few fixed sentences
("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data.", "Faster payment would help us
more than anything"), so plain patterns read them; no model, no latency."""

import re

ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]

its notes, letters, quote remarks and news (the package and the Sunday release alike), and from

    r"|restructur\w*|short-time work|lower\w* (its |their )?rating|cash is tight|we like fast payers"
    r"|negotiat\w+ with (its|their) banks|lowers our margin|loss-making|liquidity|waiting for cash",
    "spare_capacity": r"second shift has been on hold|take additional parts|looks for new customers|free (machine )?capacity"
    r"|keep (the|our) machines (busy|running)",
    "capacity_full": r"order intake is very strong|binding 12-month commitment"
    r"|cannot confirm your full forecast|fully booked|allocat\w+ (volumes|in line)|factory is super busy"
    r"|high capacity utili[sz]ation|prioriti[sz]e customers with firm",
    "open_book": r"walk (us|you) through (their|our) calculation",
    "stale_costing": r"not followed (his|its|their) material|own spreadsheet",
    "partnership_2022": r"kept supplying at the old price",
    "reference_customer": r"important reference customer",
    "approval_2pct": r"above 2 ?% need the approval|pricing committee",
    "deprioritising_us": r"reviewing small accounts|not strategic|reorganising our range"
    r"|supply from stock only|sharpens its focus|focus on customers with volume",
    "price_frozen": r"no room on price|not discounted|price list applies to all|discounts not possible"
    r"|frozen all price reductions",
    "hedged": r"bought (their|our) [\w ,]{1,40} forward|covered at fixed prices|material covered until"
    r"|secures power prices|hedged",
    "complains_late_pay": r"invoices are overdue",
}
# Cost of money per year by owner type (seen in practice: groups 4 to 7 %, family firms 7 to 8.5 %,
# founder-run job shops 12 to 17 %); a cash need adds to it.
RATE = {"group": 0.05, "private": 0.07, "family": 0.075, "founder": 0.12}
DEFAULT_RATE = 0.07


def signals_in(text):
    return sorted(k for k, pat in SIGNALS.items() if re.search(pat, text or "", re.I))


def supplier_texts(pkg, sid):
    """Every text about this supplier: its letters, call and meeting notes and news, from the
    package and the Sunday release (both reach `ids` and `document`), plus its quote remarks."""
    texts = []
    for ref in pkg.ids("doc:") + pkg.ids("news:"):
        row = pkg.lookup(ref) or {}
        if row.get("supplier") != sid and row.get("supplier_id") != sid:
            continue
        try:
            texts.append(pkg.document(ref))
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file: its headline still counts
            texts.append(" ".join(str(v) for k, v in row.items() if k in ("title", "headline", "body", "subject")))
    try:
        texts += [r.get("remarks") or "" for r in pkg.query("SELECT remarks FROM quotes WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite
        pass
    return texts


def profile(pkg, sid):
    """{owner_type, country, category, signals, rate, warm}; neutral when the package does not know it."""
    out = {"owner_type": None, "country": None, "category": None, "signals": [], "rate": DEFAULT_RATE, "warm": True}
    if pkg is None or not pkg.lookup(sid):
        return out
    try:
        sup = pkg.query("SELECT country, category, skonto_days, skonto_pct FROM suppliers WHERE id = ?", (sid,))
        intel = pkg.query("SELECT owner_type, staff FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite: neutral
        return out
    sig = signals_in("\n".join(supplier_texts(pkg, sid)))
    owner = intel[0]["owner_type"] if intel else None
    rate = RATE.get(owner, DEFAULT_RATE)
    if "cash_need" in sig:
        rate += 0.05
    if sup and sup[0].get("skonto_pct") and sup[0].get("skonto_days"):
        # a cash discount of s % for paying d days early is worth s / d * 360 % a year to it
        days_early = max(1, 30 - int(sup[0]["skonto_days"]))
        rate = max(rate, min(0.2, sup[0]["skonto_pct"] / 100 * 360 / max(days_early, 10) / 2))
    out.update(
        owner_type=owner,
        country=sup[0]["country"] if sup else None,
        category=sup[0]["category"] if sup else None,
        signals=sig,
        rate=round(rate, 3),
        warm=owner in (None, "family", "founder", "private"),
    )
    return out

"""Every case file we know (practice, hosted or not, and the sandbox) plays through arena-sim with
our agent: no exception on any case structure (bundles, 3-bidder RFQs, tooling, index clauses,
75 term combinations). The sim's supplier is a script, so this checks code paths, not tactics."""

import json
import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app

from buyer import runner

CASES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "logs" / "cases"


def all_cases():
    out = {}
    for path in sorted(CASES.glob("*.json")):
        for case in json.loads(path.read_text()):
            case = {k: v for k, v in case.items() if k != "hosted"}
            out[case["case_id"]] = case
    return out


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def arena():
    cases = all_cases()
    sim = Sim(cases, clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(sim), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    key = ArenaClient(url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    yield ArenaClient(url, key, rate=1000), cases
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case_id", sorted(all_cases()))
def test_every_case_plays_through(arena, case_id, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    client, cases = arena
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    result = runner.play_case(RemoteTable(client), case_id)
    assert "deal" in result
    if result["deal"]:
        assert 0 <= result["score"] <= 1

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **The round-1 counter is a cap plus claims, not a reaction to the anchor.**
  D01 (quote 52.90), 30 sandbox runs: anchors 44.0 to 48.5 without claims all got 51.30 (-3.0 %);
  a should-cost claim alone 51.00, the order prices alone 50.30, notice or scorecard alone 51.30,

  got less (52.30), a shallow one (50.60) 51.40. Words ("what would you need") left the counter at
  51.30 and moved the final (49.40 against 50.00). Distributors (P08, P18): anchor 0.787 of the
  quote got -8 to -10 % in 13 runs; the same sheets and claims gave 5.43 in one run and 5.57 in
  another (supplier-side noise of about 1 %); the order prices and the scorecard "do not change
  our calculation", the forecast is "taken into account" without a visible effect. → Open near
  0.8 of the quote in leverage cases (deeper buys nothing and costs patience), put the claims
  that count into round 1, and treat single-run differences under 2 % as noise.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **After round 1 each supplier concedes a capped step per round and stops
  after a fixed number of counters.** D01: caps of about 1.6 %, 0.8 %, 0.6 %, 0.4 %, 0.2 % in
  rounds 2 to 6 (0.8 x our move below the cap), final offer in round 6 at the latest or right
  after a move of ours under 0.1 %. Donautal and Werdenfels: 3 counters (r2 +0.04 to +0.20, r3
  0 to +0.15), final in round 2 after a +1 % move, in round 3 after 30 % of the gap, in round 4
  after three 30 % moves (P08 `f9e9b6dc7ed8e47d`); a move of 55 % of the gap got a hold and a
  higher price (P08 `5d30fbf219bdc50a` 5.55 to 5.58, P18 `f038c7d05bfee4d6`). Leitner (P07):
  3 counters of 3.5 %, 2.2 %, 1.1 %, final in round 3 in all 5 runs. Nordmark (P02): 4 counters
  of 0.93, 0.88, 0.30, 0.07 EUR at a cumulative gap of only 0.03, its reason "as you cannot
  commit to a binding higher volume, our flexibility is exhausted". Kalwisz (P11): three steps
  of 0.50 then holds at 45.50 "for 300 ppm and 0 chargeback" (it priced 300 ppm at +0.50 over
  1500 ppm, `587fe8dcbf9f6c9c`). Ravensteiner (P10): 2 counters. → The round count, not the
  gap, ends most threads: make every round count, move 25 to 35 % of the gap, never under 1 %
  and never over 50 %.

  C_best, relationship charge 0): P08 5.10 fixed at 90 days, 24 or 36 months (5.06 with the 5 %

"""The Live Final loop end to end on arena-sim: waves appear one after another in the case list,
every case of a wave plays within its cap, a poll error is polled again, and the loop ends when
the last wave has closed. No network, no model."""

import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

from buyer import runner


class FinalClient(ArenaClient):
    """The sim's client with a scripted final: `cases("final")` is 403 before the first wave, then
    lists each wave's cases as open with seconds left, then as closed; one poll fails outright."""

    def __init__(self, url, key, waves):
        super().__init__(url, key, rate=1000)
        self.waves, self.polls = waves, 0

    def cases(self, set_="practice"):
        if set_ != "final":
            return super().cases(set_)
        self.polls += 1
        if self.polls == 1:
            raise ArenaError(403, "the final has not started")
        if self.polls == 3:
            raise ArenaError(500, "a hiccup")
        wave = min(1 + (self.polls - 2) // 2, len(self.waves))  # a new wave every second poll
        out = []
        for w, ids in enumerate(self.waves, start=1):
            if w > wave:
                continue
            open_ = w == wave
            for cid in ids:
                out.append({"case_id": cid, "wave": w, "open": open_, "seconds_left": 480 if open_ else 0})
        return out


@pytest.fixture
def sim_url():
    sim = Sim(load_cases(), clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(sim), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


def test_play_waves_plays_every_wave(sim_url, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    key = ArenaClient(sim_url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    waves = [["case:S01", "case:S02"], ["case:S03"]]
    client = FinalClient(sim_url, key, waves)
    out = runner.play_waves(client, waves=2, parallel=3, poll=0.05)
    assert set(out) == {"case:S01", "case:S02", "case:S03"}
    for case_id, result in out.items():
        assert not isinstance(result, Exception), (case_id, result)
        assert "deal" in result
